title: smart-routing-fallback-incident-breadcrumbs-nora
content:
Summary:
Saw an automated regional failover (us-east-1 -> eu-west-1) triggered for a subset of tenants between 2025-03-10T14:02Z and 2025-03-10T14:20Z. Traffic was routed to fallback model variants even though capacity in primary region was available. Goal: capture commands tried, raw errors, hypotheses, and immediate next actions for the oncall handoff.

Timeline + quick notes:
- 2025-03-10T14:00Z — Alerts: increased 5xxs (502/503) on /v1/generate for some tenants, spike in fallback rate metric (route.fallback.count).
- 14:05Z — Smart-router started emitting "fallback-invoked" logs with policy=latency_based and reason="no healthy backends" for tenant cluster T-332.
- 14:10Z — Canary probes showed primary region pod readiness OK; but route decision table showed zero eligible backends for the policy.
- 14:18Z — Manual reroute (force route policy=cost_aware) sent, traffic normalized.

Commands run (raw):
- k8s / router / logs
  kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=smart-router -o wide
  kubectl -n infra logs deploy/smart-router --since=20m | grep "fallback-invoked" -n -B2 -A4

  Example output snippet we captured:
  "2025-03-10T14:05:11Z router[proc-3] INFO fallback-invoked tenant=T-332 policy=latency_based reason=\"no healthy backends\" selected_variant=redwood-quantized-v1 region=us-east-1 trace_id=abcd-1234
   node_selection_count=0 eligible_nodes=[]"

- health checks against backends
  # probe agent on one of the cpuserving nodes from router pod
  curl -sS -H 'Host: backend-123.internal' http://10.2.4.11:8080/healthz -v
  > HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  > {"status":"ok","uptime":"12h"}

- routing decision table (redis/kv) inspection
  redis-cli -h redis-infra.hq HGET route:tenant:T-332 policy:latency_based
  # returned: "[]"  <-- suspicious (should list eligible node ids)

- direct list of backends registered
  redis-cli -h redis-infra.hq SMEMBERS backends:us-east-1:active
  # returned: "[\"node-17\", \"node-19\"]"  (so nodes *are* registered)

- tried forcing policy refresh to see if stale cache -> decision would update
  curl -X POST "https://config.redwood/api/v1/flush-routing-cache?tenant=T-332" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ME"
  # response: 200 {"status":"ok","flushed":true}
  # no immediate change in router logs; subsequent decision still empty for that policy

Error snippets / interesting log lines:
- "eligible_nodes=[]" repeated despite backends present in backends:us-east-1:active set.
- "policy-eval-timeout": some policy eval spans hanging for > 150ms before timing out and marking as ineligible.
- Route decision service returned HTTP 204 for /v1/decide?policy=latency_based&tenant=T-332 (empty body) — we interpret as no eligible nodes.
- Trace span id abcd-1234 shows decision-service returned early with status 204, upstream node check logs show late response from health-check/filter stage.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Policy-evaluator timeout regression: recent change in policy-eval path (PR #8345) added an extra HTTP call to region-metadata service that is intermittently slow. When policy-eval times out it treats candidate list as empty -> triggers fallback.
   - Evidence: policy-eval-timeout traces, a PR touching the same module merged 1 day before.

2) Cache inconsistency between backends set and policy decision cache: backends are registered, but the policy-evaluator reads from a cached index that can be stale after rapid churn.
   - Evidence: TTL on cache keys is short but we saw no refresh after cache flush call (maybe wrong cache namespace).

3) Feature-flag evaluated endpoint off by region: new rollout of region-aware weights accidentally set region weight to 0 for some tenants (weight=0 -> excluded).
   - Evidence: some tenant-specific overrides exist in LaunchDarkly / config; need to check flag states for T-332.

4) Clock skew affecting TTL checks: if router node clock ahead/behind, it might consider nodes expired.
   - Evidence: NTP logs show slight offset on node-19 (~6s) not enough but mentioned for completeness.

Repro steps tried (so far):
- Replayed a subset of requests with header X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1 and watched router decision log -> still empty decision for policy=latency_based (so not client header issue).
- Direct invocation of policy-evaluator with same inputs (trace id, tenant, policy) returned 204 when called from router pod; called from my laptop returned 200 (lists nodes). Suggests something environmental (network / pod config) causing slow remote call inside cluster.
  curl -v "http://policy-eval.internal/v1/decide?tenant=T-332&policy=latency_based" -H "X-Request-Id: local-test-1"

What changed recently (context):
- PR #8345 merged to policy-eval path 2025-03-09 (adds call to region-metadata service for weight adjustments).
- Autoscaling burst yesterday caused several backend nodes to be terminated/started in quick succession for T-332 (high churn).
- Small config change to reduce policy-eval timeout from 200ms -> 150ms in config release 2025-03-09.

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Flushed routing cache: no effect.
- Increased policy-eval timeout to 300ms via config toggle for routing namespace (rolled to 20% -> monitor).
- Allowed traffic to fallback policy=cost_aware (manual override) -> normalized errors but with increased latency/cost.

Notes from traces (trace abcd-1234):
- span: policy-eval start -> calls region-metadata (duration 210ms) -> region-metadata responds 210ms -> policy-eval hits 150ms timeout -> returns 204 (empty).
- This exact timing explains fallback.

Immediate next steps / TODO (assignments):
- (Samir) Rollback PR #8345 in staging & run policy-eval microbench to confirm latency regression (ASAP).
- (Amara) Check LaunchDarkly flags for tenant overrides T-332 and validate no region weight=0 overrides (check audit log around 2025-03-09).
- (Ethan) Backfill metric to capture policy-eval remote call latencies vs timeout and create alert when remote-call > 100ms.
- (Nora - me) Monitor the 20% timeout increase experiment: if fallback count drops back to baseline within 15 mins, promote to 100%. If not, revert and continue investigation.

Follow-ups to add to postmortem if confirmed:
- Revert the timeout reduction change or implement bulkhead/async remote call pattern so decision doesn't fail on non-critical slow ops.
- Add integration test to simulate region-metadata slowness and assert policy-eval degrades gracefully (doesn't return empty candidate list).
- Improve observability: record which sub-call in policy-eval caused the timeout and expose per-tenant failure counters.

Misc notes / scratch ideas:
- Consider changing decision semantics: if non-critical weight adjustment service times out, fallback to using last-known weights instead of emptying the candidate list.
- Maybe add a short-lived local memoization layer in router pod for last-known decisions for each tenant (stale-while-revalidate).

If you're taking over oncall: look at trace abcd-1234 (console link above), grep router logs for "policy-eval-timeout" between 2025-03-10T13:50Z and 14:30Z. Contact me on slack @nora for context.

End of notes.
